tools.name: ping
tools.description: Health check for the Hey Anon MCP server. Returns "pong" and the server time (ISO 8601). No API key required.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Sign in to Hey Anon (or create an account) without an API key, through Privy in the browser. Returns a link and a short code. tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Check which Hey Anon account the API key of this connection belongs to: account id, account type (e.g. privy), Privy user id, creation date, and the number of wallets per type. Use it to verify a login (an authenticated call; ping alone does not prove the key works). Read-only.

tools.name: wallet_list
tools.description: List the user wallets registered in Hey Anon: display name, type (evm, solana, ton, etc.), address, labels and whether the wallet is archived. tools.name: ask_gemma
tools.description: Ask Gemma, the Hey Anon crypto research assistant: protocol analysis, community and social insights, market data, news, token analytics by contract address. tools.name: isProcessing
tools.description: Check whether Anon is still processing the previous ask_anon request. Returns "isProcessing: true|false". Use before sending another message, or when a request looks stuck (then call abort).

tools.name: abort
tools.description: Force-stop Anon processing of the current ask_anon request. Use only when isProcessing stays true for too long or the request is stuck; otherwise keep polling anon_message until the message is done.

tools.name: projects
tools.description: List the protocols and integrations Anon can operate (swaps, lending, staking, bridges, CEX, etc.): name, key, description, supported networks, tool count. Use it to check whether Anon supports a protocol or network before asking.

tools.name: scheduled_task_list
tools.description: List the user scheduled tasks: automations created through Anon that run at a given time or when a price condition is met. There is no create/update tool: to create an automation, ask Anon via ask_anon (e.g. "Buy 0.1 ETH on Base when ETH drops below 2000"), then use this tool to confirm it exists. R

tools.name: scheduled_task_get
tools.description: Get one scheduled task by id (from scheduled_task_list). Returns id, description, status, type and taskExecutorResponse (the last execution result).

tools.name: scheduled_task_delete
tools.description: Delete (cancel) a scheduled task by id. Irreversible: the automation will not run again. Returns a confirmation.

tools.name: portfolio_tokens
tools.description: Token balances for every user wallet (addresses taken from wallet_list) across all supported networks. Returns JSON [{ walletAddress, data }]; for EVM wallets data.evm is keyed by chain id, Solana balances are in data.solana. Output can be large with many wallets.

tools.name: portfolio_transactions
tools.description: Recent transactions for every user wallet (addresses taken from wallet_list). Returns JSON [{ walletAddress, data }]. Output can be large with many wallets.

tools.name: portfolio_defi
tools.description: DeFi positions (LP, staking, lending, vaults, etc.) for every user wallet (addresses taken from wallet_list). Returns JSON [{ walletAddress, data }].

tools.name: portfolio_cex
tools.description: Balances and positions from the exchange accounts linked to Hey Anon (e.g. Hyperliquid, keyed by exchange). Pass address (an EVM wallet from wallet_list) when the user has several EVM wallets, otherwise the backend rejects the call. Returns the raw JSON response.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "ask_anon" is 1699 chars, far longer than this server's median (278). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "address_book_list" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: login, ask_anon, isProcessing, anon_message · Private data: ping, login, login_status, whoami, wallet_list, ask_anon, ask_gemma, portfolio_tokens, portfolio_transactions, portfolio_defi, portfolio_cex, anon_message, transfer_native, transfer_asset · Public sink: login, ask_anon, transfer_native, transfer_asset, address_book_list · Destructive: ask_anon, scheduled_task_list, scheduled_task_delete, anon_message.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: login, ask_anon, isProcessing, anon_message · Private data: ping, login, login_status, whoami, wallet_list, ask_anon, ask_gemma, portfolio_tokens, portfolio_transactions, portfolio_defi, portfolio_cex, anon_message, transfer_native, transfer_asset · Public sink: login, ask_anon, transfer_native, transfer_asset, address_book_list · Destructive: ask_anon, scheduled_task_list, scheduled_task_delete, anon_message

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
